# Serve the CLI's commands as tools over MCP, with code mode

## Intent

An agent whose harness speaks MCP can do what the `parley` CLI does (see
who else is working, fork, read and commit, open and land a change, drive a
sandbox) as tool calls, by starting `parley mcp` on its own machine. With
code mode it does a whole sequence of them in one call, and with a sandbox
named, the same script mixes hub operations with file, search and shell
work in that sandbox. The tools are the commands themselves, so the CLI and
the tools cannot drift apart.

## Goals

1. `parley mcp` serves one MCP session on standard input and output, and a
   harness started with it lists and calls tools with no other setup than
   the CLI's own endpoint and credential.
2. Every served tool is one CLI command: its name, description, parameters
   and result come from the command's declaration, and calling it does what
   running the command does.
3. By default the tools are the commands an agent uses, at most 80 of them;
   the operator of the harness changes the selection with one flag; and
   commands that administer the hub or handle credentials are never served.
4. One `code_mode` call can run a script that makes several tool calls,
   some concurrently, and returns only what the script prints and returns.
5. With `--sandbox`, the sandbox's tools are served beside the hub tools
   and are callable from the same script.
6. The `parley` binary still builds without a C toolchain.

## Non-goals

- Serving MCP from the hub for hub operations. `parley mcp` runs where the
  agent runs; the hub runs no model-written script.
- MCP over HTTP from the CLI. Standard input and output only.
- New hub routes. Everything goes through routes that exist, and through
  the sandbox tool routes of PRD 18.
- Tools that are not commands, and commands invented for tools.
- A model loop, prompts, resources, sampling or elicitation.
- Serving the tools of more than one sandbox in one session.
- Changing what any command does when run from the shell.

## Background

`parley` declares every command through one helper (ADR 02,
`internal/cli/command.go`): its words, description, route, named arguments,
flags with type, default and description, and its `auth` level. The same
declaration drives the command and its JSON help: `parley help --json`
lists 171 commands today in 28 groups (the first word), each with `name`,
`description`, `method`, `path`, `args`, `flags` and `auth`. Flag types are
`bool`, `string`, `stringArray`, `int`, `integer` and `duration`. Every
command prints one JSON document or nothing on stdout, and every error is
one envelope, the hub's or one of the CLI's five types (`usage_error`,
`client_error`, `wait_failed`, `wait_timeout`, `condition_not_met`).

So a tool definition for each command already exists in all but form.
What does not exist is a way for a harness to use it: today an agent shells
out to `parley` and parses stdout, one process per operation.

Group sizes today: `change` 25, `admin` 22, `sandbox` 19, `scm` 11,
`workspace` 11, `issue` 9, `patch` 8, `pr` 7, `rebuild` 7, `tokens` 7,
`forge` 5, `vars` 5, `claim` 4, `fork` 4, `secrets` 4, `keys` 3, `orgs` 3,
`policy` 3, `events` 2, `land` 2, `rerere` 2, `user` 2, and `activity`,
`credential-helper`, `help`, `label`, `login`, `version` 1 each.

Code mode is agentkit-go's `codemode` package: one tool that runs a
model-written Starlark script whose functions are other tools. The script
has no file system, network or clock; it reaches the world only through the
tools bound to it, and its description declares each bound tool as a typed
function, so its size grows with the number of tools. agentkit-go's
`mcpserve` serves a runner's tools over MCP on stdio. Linking these today
needs cgo and the model providers' SDKs; agentkit-go's PRD 16 removes both
costs, and this PRD waits for it.

PRD 18 gives a sandbox whose profile names a tool server two REST routes:
`GET …/sandboxes/:id/tools` lists the caller's tool set with schemas, and
`POST …/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name` makes one call.

## Requirements

### The command

`parley mcp` is declared like every command (ADR 02), with `auth` level
`user`. It resolves the endpoint and the credential as every command does,
before it serves anything.

- Without an endpoint or a credential it ends as any command does: a
  `client_error` envelope on stderr, exit status 2, and nothing on stdout.
- It then serves one MCP session until the client closes its end, and
  exits 0. Only protocol frames go to stdout; one line per tool call
  (tool, outcome, duration, never arguments or results) goes to stderr.
- `initialize` answers with the server name `parley`, the CLI's version and
  instructions of at most three sentences: what the tools are, the fixed
  workspace and sandbox when given, and that `code_mode` chains them.
- SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the session and cancels running calls.
- `parley mcp --list` prints the tools it would serve as one JSON array of
  `{name, description, input_schema}` and exits 0, without starting a
  session. With `--sandbox` it includes the sandbox's tools.
- The credential is read once at start. The hub's `401` on a later call is
  that call's tool error.

### Which commands are tools

`--groups` selects command groups, comma-separated. A group name alone
serves all of the group's commands; `name:read` serves only those whose
route's method is `GET`. The default is
`activity,change,claim,fork,land,sandbox,scm,workspace:read`.

- **Never served**, whatever `--groups` says: the groups `admin`, `keys`,
  `tokens`, `secrets`, `login`, `credential-helper`, `help` and `version`;
  `mcp` itself; every command whose `auth` is `admin` or `none`; every
  command that shows a secret once; and every command that needs a
  terminal or runs until interrupted (`sandbox shell`, `events tail`).
  Naming a never-served group in `--groups` is a `usage_error` that names
  it.
- An unknown group name is a `usage_error` listing the group names.
- `--read-only` narrows whatever is selected to `GET` commands, and with
  `--sandbox` asks for nothing more than the sandbox's read-only set.
- More than 150 tools after selection is a `usage_error` saying how many
  and to narrow `--groups`.
- A command added to a served group later is a tool without further work.

### How a command becomes a tool

- **Name.** The command's words joined by `_`, with `-` replaced by `_`:
  `change land` is `change_land`.
- **Description.** The command's description.
- **Parameters.** One per named argument (a string, required as the
  command requires it) and one per flag, typed by the flag's type
  (`stringArray` is an array of strings; `duration` is a string such as
  `90s`), with the flag's description. Flag names keep their words with
  `-` replaced by `_`. Left out: `api-key`, `endpoint-url`, `json` and
  `poll-interval`, and any flag that makes a command run until
  interrupted (`follow` of `sandbox logs`; `follow` of `scm log`, which
  follows renames, stays).
- **`--workspace <slug>`** makes the `slug` parameter of every tool
  optional, with that workspace as its value when left out. A fork's slug
  can still be passed.
- **The call.** The tool runs the command's own run step in the `parley
  mcp` process, with the given arguments and flags and JSON output.
- **The result.** A command that prints a JSON object succeeds with that
  object as the tool's data. Any other JSON value is `{"result": value}`.
  A command that prints nothing is `{}`.
- **Errors.** An error envelope is a failed tool result, not a protocol
  error: `error` is the envelope's `error_type` (or `http_<code>` when the
  hub gave none), `detail` its message. The CLI's own error types are
  failed results with that type as `error`. A parameter that is not in the
  schema or has the wrong type is `usage_error`, and nothing is sent.
- **No standard input.** A tool never reads stdin or a terminal. A value
  of `-` where the command would read stdin is `usage_error`. No command
  asks a question on a terminal: one that destroys data requires its
  `confirm` flag, which is the tool's `confirm` parameter, and without it
  the call is `usage_error` as from the shell.
- **Waiting.** A command with `--wait` waits inside the tool call, bounded
  by its `timeout` parameter as from the shell.
- **Local files.** A command that reads or writes a local path
  (`sandbox upload`, `sandbox download`) does so on the machine where
  `parley mcp` runs, relative to its working directory.
- A tool call is bounded at 30 minutes; past it the call is cancelled and
  fails with `error: "timeout"`.

### Code mode

`code_mode` is served after the other tools and is bound to all of them.

- Its rules and limits are agentkit-go's, except the script's wall time,
  which is 10 minutes by default and set with `--script-timeout` (from 1
  second to 30 minutes; outside that is a `usage_error`).
- Every call a script makes is a tool call like a direct one: same
  parameters, same result, one stderr line each.
- `--no-code-mode` leaves it out.
- At start `parley mcp` writes one line to stderr with the number of tools
  and the size of the `code_mode` description in bytes.

### A sandbox's tools

`--sandbox <id>` names one sandbox of the workspace given with
`--workspace`, which is then required (`usage_error` without it).

- At start the tools are read from the hub (`GET …/sandboxes/:id/tools`).
  If that fails, `parley mcp` ends with the hub's error envelope on stderr
  and exit status 1: a sandbox without tools (`tools_unavailable`), not
  ready, unknown, or not accessible.
- Each sandbox tool is served under its own name, description and input
  schema, after the command tools and before `code_mode`, and is bound to
  `code_mode`.
- A call is one `POST …/tools/:name`. The hub's `{ok, data, error,
  detail, text}` is the tool's result as it is. A hub error (the sandbox
  stopped, a limit) is a failed result with its `error_type`.
- A sandbox tool whose name equals a command tool's is an error at start
  naming both, exit status 2.
- The set is the one the hub gives the credential: the full set, or the
  read-only set. With `--read-only`, tools of the full set that are not in
  the read-only set are not served.

### End-to-end flows

1. **An agent lands a change.** A harness starts
   `parley mcp --workspace demo`. The agent calls `activity`, then
   `fork_create`, then one `code_mode` script that commits two files with
   `scm_commit` on the fork, opens the change with `change_open` and lands
   it with `change_land` with `wait` set; the script returns the landed
   sha. The hub's audit shows the same requests the shell commands make.
2. **Hub and sandbox in one script.** Started with `--workspace demo--fix
   --sandbox sbx_…`, a script runs `search_files` and `edit_file` in the
   sandbox, `execute` to run the tests and push, then `change_show` on the
   hub, and returns the change's state.
3. **A read-only assistant.** Started with `--read-only`, the tool list
   holds only reading commands, and `change_land` is not in it.
4. **A refusal.** `parley mcp --groups admin` prints a `usage_error` and
   exits 2.

## Design Decisions

1. **The tools are generated from the command declarations** (my decision,
   following ADR 02): one source for the shell, the JSON help and the
   tools.
2. **The agent groups are direct tools and are bound to code mode;
   `--groups` changes the selection** (owner's decision).
3. **`--sandbox` adds one sandbox's tools** (owner's decision).
4. **`--workspace` is optional** (owner's decision). It makes `slug`
   optional with a default instead of removing the parameter: an agent
   that forks has to name the fork, which a removed parameter would
   prevent.
5. **`parley` stays pure Go; agentkit-go is slimmed first** (owner's
   decision). This PRD waits for agentkit-go's PRD 16.
6. **`group:read` instead of a special case for `workspace`**: the default
   wants the workspace reads without archive and delete, and the same
   suffix is useful for every group.
7. **Never-served commands are decided by rule, not by list**, so a new
   admin or secret-showing command is excluded without anyone remembering
   to.
8. **Sandbox tools keep their names** (`read_file`, not
   `sandbox_read_file`): models know them, and command tools always carry
   their group as a prefix, so a clash is unlikely and is an error.
9. **No guard of the CLI's own on `execute`**: it runs in the sandbox, and
   the hub's rules for the route decide who may call it.
10. **Script wall time 10 minutes**, not code mode's 30 seconds: one
    `change_land` with `wait` can take minutes.
11. **Constraint: MCP and code mode come from agentkit-go** (`mcpserve`,
    `codemode`, `runner`), not from new code in Parley.
12. **One package, profile `full`** (decided when the package was
    written): six requirements and five tasks. The first two tasks, the
    selection with `--list` and the call of a command tool, need nothing of
    agentkit-go; the session, code mode and the sandbox's tools do.
13. **The numbers of the Background are the code's today**: `parley help
    --json` lists 186 commands in 31 groups, the groups `webhook`,
    `session` and `audit` among them, and the default selection is 69
    tools. Flags also have the type `int64`, which is an integer
    parameter like `int` and `integer`.
14. **A parameter's name** is the argument's or the flag's name in lower
    case with every character that is not a letter or a digit replaced by
    `_`: `sandbox-path` is `sandbox_path`, `KEY=VALUE` is `key_value`.
15. **`--workspace` gives its value to the workspace argument under each of
    its names**: the commands call it `slug`, `workspace-slug`,
    `WORKSPACE`, or `parent` (`fork create`). All four become optional
    with the workspace as their value when left out; the PRD names only
    `slug`, which would leave the sandbox commands and `fork_create`
    without the default.
16. **"Shows a secret once" is the declaration's `ShowsOnce`**, which only
    commands of `keys` and `tokens` set today. `fork create` can mint a
    token and stays a tool: the agent that forks needs it, and the PRD's
    first flow calls it.
17. **A command that needs a terminal or runs until interrupted, and a
    flag that makes one run until interrupted, is marked in its
    declaration**, so that the rule of decision 7 holds for commands added
    later: `sandbox shell`, `events tail` and the `follow` flag of
    `sandbox logs` carry the mark today.
18. **The lines on stderr are JSON**, one object per line, as every other
    line `parley` writes there: `{"tool", "ok", "error"?, "duration_ms"}`
    for a call, and `{"tools", "code_mode_description_bytes"}` at start
    (`code_mode_description_bytes` is `0` with `--no-code-mode`).
19. **With `--read-only`, a sandbox's tools `write_file`, `edit_file`,
    `execute` and `run_command` are not served**: the hub lists only the
    caller's own set, and PRD 18 defines the read-only set as the full set
    without those four.
20. **`parley mcp` is tested at two levels**: the tools and their calls
    in-process through the runner (`Call`), and the session over standard
    input and output through the built binary, since `ServeStdio` reads
    the process's own standard input.

## Dependencies

- ADR 02 (`docs/adr/02-declare-every-cli-command-through-one-helper.md`)
  and package 09 `cli_foundation`: the declarations this reads. `mcp` is
  declared through the same helper.
- PRD 18, package 56 `sandbox_tool_routes` (active, every task done): the
  two REST routes `--sandbox` uses. Everything but `--sandbox` works
  without it.
- agentkit-go PRD 16 (in pull request 185 of that repository, not built):
  the runner, code mode and MCP serving without cgo and providers. Hard
  dependency.
- Package 49 `agent_sessions_and_usage` (active, every task done): its
  `session` commands are a group like any other and can be named in
  `--groups`; the default list does not name them.

## Verified External API

`github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go`, read in its checkout
(`docs/generated/` and `go doc`):

- `core.Tool` is a struct with `Name`, `Description`,
  `InputSchema *schema.Schema`, `OutputSchema *schema.Schema`,
  `ReachableTools []Tool`, `Handler ToolHandler`, `Execute ResultHandler`.
- `core.ToolResult` has `OK bool`, `Data map[string]any`, `Error string`,
  `Detail string`; `core.OKResult(data map[string]any) ToolResult` and
  `core.ErrResult(code, detail string) ToolResult`.
- `codemode.New(tools []core.Tool, opts codemode.Options) (core.Tool, codemode.BuildInfo, error)`;
  `Options` has `MaxTimeout`, `MaxSteps`, `MaxCalls`,
  `MaxConcurrentCalls`, `MaxOutputBytes`; `BuildInfo` has
  `DescriptionBytes`, `DescriptionChars`, `BoundToolsCount`.
- `agentkit.NewRunner(ts agentkit.Toolset) (*agentkit.Runner, error)`;
  `Toolset` has `Tools`, `Policy`, `Guard`, `After`, `Events`. A reachable
  tool named `execute` or `run_command` needs a `Guard`
  (`guard.AllowAll` exists).
- `mcpserve.New(r *agentkit.Runner, opts mcpserve.Options) (*mcpserve.Server, error)`
  and `(*Server).ServeStdio(ctx context.Context) error`; `Options` has
  `Name`, `Version`, `Instructions`, `Logger`. `ServeStdio` closes
  `os.Stdin` when the session ends.

Read the same way when the package was written, in the checkout at
`v0.9.1-40-gd77347b`:

- `type ToolHandler func(ctx context.Context, input json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error)`
  and `type ResultHandler func(ctx context.Context, input json.RawMessage) ToolResult`;
  exactly one of `Tool.Handler` and `Tool.Execute` must be set.
- `core.ToolResult` also has `Text string`, the model-facing text.
- `schema.Parse(data []byte) (*schema.Schema, error)` builds a schema from
  a JSON schema document; `schema.Object`, `schema.Prop`, `schema.Opt`,
  `schema.String`, `schema.Bool`, `schema.Int` and `schema.Array` build one
  in code.
- `(*agentkit.Runner).Call(ctx context.Context, name string, input json.RawMessage) core.ToolResult`
  and `(*agentkit.Runner).Reachable() []core.Tool`.
- `mcpserve` is a module of its own,
  `github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve`.
- `mcp.CommandTransport{Command *exec.Cmd}` of
  `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` v1.8.0, which `go.mod` holds
  since package 56, is the client transport the session's tests use.

**Not built**: package `runner` and `runner.New` (agentkit-go PRD 16); the
signatures above are today's, under the root package. Today `codemode`
depends on 15 tree-sitter and provider packages and `mcpserve` on 62, so
linking them needs cgo: **this package cannot meet goal 6, and tasks 3 to 5
cannot be implemented, until agentkit-go PRD 16 is built and released.**
**Unverified**: whether `mcpserve` serves a `core.Tool` with only `Execute`
set (the runner's contract says it runs one).

## Glossary

- **Command tool**: a tool generated from one CLI command's declaration.
- **Sandbox tool**: a tool of a sandbox's tool set (PRD 18), relayed by
  `parley mcp` to the hub.
- **Group**: the first word of a command (`change`, `scm`).
- **Code mode**: the `code_mode` tool, which runs a Starlark script whose
  functions are the other served tools.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Choose which commands are tools

**Rationale:** The operator of a harness decides with one flag what its agent may do, and commands that administer the hub or handle credentials are never among it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN parley mcp --list is run, THE parley CLI SHALL print the tools it would serve as one JSON array of {name, description, input_schema}, the command tools in the order of their names and code_mode last, and exit 0 without starting a session, sending a request or reading standard input
   → exit status 0; stdout is one JSON array; with the default selection it holds the 69 command tools of the groups activity, change, claim, fork, land, sandbox and scm and of the GET commands of workspace, at most 80, and then code_mode
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, with a stubHub and probeEnv: code, out, _ = runCLI(t, "mcp", "--list"); code == 0; names(out) hold change_land, scm_commit, fork_create, activity, sandbox_exec and workspace_get, and not workspace_delete; every name but the last is a command of the default groups in help --json; the last is code_mode; len(names) <= 81; hub.requests is empty
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHERE --groups names command groups, separated by commas, each as name or as name:read, THE parley CLI SHALL serve all commands of a group named alone and only the commands whose route's method is GET of a group named with :read, in place of the default selection activity,change,claim,fork,land,sandbox,scm,workspace:read
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table over --groups with --list: {"scm": every scm command; "scm:read": the scm commands whose method is GET, not scm_commit; "issue,pr:read": every issue command and the GET commands of pr; "workspace": workspace_delete among them; none given: the default}; each compared with the commands help --json lists for the group
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE parley CLI SHALL for any selection, never serve the command mcp, a command of the groups admin, keys, tokens, secrets, login, credential-helper, help and version, a command whose auth is admin or none, a command whose declaration says it shows a secret once, or a command whose declaration says it needs a terminal or runs until interrupted (sandbox shell, events tail)
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go: with --groups naming every group that may be named (from help --json), --list holds no sandbox_shell, no events_tail, no mcp, and no tool whose command has auth admin or none; with probe commands added through options.extra in a probe group, one with ShowsOnce and one marked as needing a terminal are not listed and their plain sibling is
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF --groups names one of the never-served groups admin, keys, tokens, secrets, login, credential-helper, help, version or mcp, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL refuse to start and name the group
   → one usage_error envelope on stderr whose message names the group; exit status 2; nothing on stdout; no request sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table over the nine groups, each alone, with :read, and after a served group ("scm,admin"): code == 2; stderr is one envelope with error_type usage_error naming the group; stdout is empty; with and without --list
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF --groups names a group no command has, has an empty element, or has a suffix other than :read, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL refuse to start and list the group names
   → one usage_error envelope on stderr whose message lists the names of the groups that may be named; exit status 2; nothing on stdout
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table over --groups {"nope", "scm,,change", "scm:write", ""}: code == 2; error_type usage_error; the message holds scm and change and not admin
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHERE --read-only is given, THE parley CLI SHALL narrow whatever is selected to the commands whose route's method is GET
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go: --read-only --list holds change_show and scm_log and none of change_land, scm_commit, fork_create, sandbox_exec; --read-only --groups scm --list equals --groups scm:read --list
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] IF the selection holds more than 150 tools, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL refuse to start, say how many there are and to narrow --groups
   → one usage_error envelope on stderr whose message holds the number of tools and --groups; exit status 2; a selection of exactly 150 is served
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, with a probe group of n generated commands (options.extra) and --no-code-mode: n == 150 lists 150 tools; n == 151 is code 2, usage_error, the message holds 151 and --groups
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] THE parley CLI SHALL for any command declared in a served group, serve it as a tool with no change to parley mcp
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go: a probe command added to the group scm through options.extra, declared with declare, is listed as scm_<name> by mcp --list with its arguments and flags as parameters
   ```

### REQ-2: Make a tool definition of a command's declaration

**Rationale:** The tools are the commands themselves, so the CLI and the tools cannot drift apart.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] THE parley CLI SHALL for any served command, name its tool with the command's words joined by _ with every - replaced by _, and describe it with the command's description
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, for every tool of mcp --list with every nameable group: its name and description equal those of one command of help --json under the mapping (change land → change_land, a word with - → _), and no two tools share a name
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE parley CLI SHALL for any served command, give its tool an input schema that is an object with one string parameter per named argument, required as the command requires it, and one parameter per flag, typed by the flag's type (bool a boolean; string and duration a string; stringArray an array of strings; int, int64 and integer an integer), required when the flag is required, described by the flag's description, each named in lower case with every character that is not a letter or a digit replaced by _, and with no other parameter allowed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table of tools from mcp --list: {change_land: slug and number required strings, wait boolean, stack boolean, timeout string, expected_version string; scm_commit: put, delete and move arrays of strings, message string; sandbox_upload: workspace_slug, id, local_path, sandbox_path required; a probe command with flags of every type, an int64 and a required one among them, and the argument KEY=VALUE: key_value}; each schema has additionalProperties false and the flag's description
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE parley CLI SHALL for any served command, leave out of its tool the flags api-key, endpoint-url, json and poll-interval, and any flag its declaration marks as making the command run until interrupted
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go: no tool of mcp --list has a parameter api_key, endpoint_url, json or poll_interval; sandbox_logs has no follow; scm_log has follow; change_land has wait and timeout
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHERE --workspace <slug> is given, THE parley CLI SHALL make the workspace parameter of every tool (slug, workspace_slug, workspace or parent) optional, with that workspace as its value when a call leaves it out, while a call may still pass another slug
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, with the tools built for --workspace demo over a stubHub: slug of change_show, workspace_slug of sandbox_get and parent of fork_create are not required, and are required without --workspace; a call of change_show {number: "3"} requests /workspaces/demo/changes/3; a call with slug demo--t1 requests /workspaces/demo--t1/changes/3
   ```

### REQ-3: Run the command when its tool is called

**Rationale:** Calling a tool does what running the command does, so an agent that knows the CLI knows the tools.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a command tool is called with parameters its schema allows, THE parley CLI SHALL run the command's own run step in the parley mcp process with the endpoint and credential resolved at start, the parameters as its arguments and flags, and JSON output, and give what the command prints as the tool's result
   → the hub receives the request the command sends from the shell with the same arguments; a JSON object printed is the result's data, any other JSON value v is {"result": v}, nothing printed is {}; ok is true; nothing is written to the session's stdout by the command
   Check: integration
   - setup: a stubHub and the tools built with its URL and a credential
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, calling tools through the runner's Call: {change_show {slug, number}: the stub's object is data, and the recorded request equals the one runCLI("change", "show", …) records, method, path, query and Authorization; scm_commit with put ["a=1", "b=2"] and message: the body equals the shell's; a command that answers a JSON array: data == {"result": [...]}; a command whose answer has no body and no confirm document: data == {}}
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the hub answers a command's request with an error, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL give a failed tool result and not a protocol error
   → ok false; error is the envelope's error_type, or http_<code> when the hub gave none; detail is the envelope's message; the session goes on
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table over the stub's answer to change_show: {404 with the envelope change_not_found: error change_not_found and its message; 401 unauthenticated: error unauthenticated; 502 with a body that is not an envelope: error http_502}; ok == false in each; a later call succeeds
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the command ends with one of the CLI's own errors: usage_error, client_error, wait_failed, wait_timeout or condition_not_met, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL give a failed tool result with that type, as from the shell, a command that destroys data and is called without its confirm parameter included
   → ok false; error is the CLI's error type; detail its message; for workspace_delete without confirm, error usage_error and no request sent
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/cli/mcp_test.go, a table: {workspace_delete {slug} without confirm (--groups workspace): usage_error, no request; with confirm true: the DELETE is sent; activity with fail_on_overlap and an overlapping answer: condition_not_met with the answer as data; a hub that cannot be reached: client_error}
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a call carries a parameter that is not in the tool's schema, one of the wrong type, or lacks a required one, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL refuse the call and send nothing

1. [REQ-3.6] WHEN a tool of a command with --wait is called with wait true, THE parley CLI SHALL wait inside the call for the operation to end, bounded by the call's timeout parameter as from the shell

In test/e2e/cli_test.go, in the session test: the initialize result's serverInfo is parley with the built version

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent lands a change through tool calls

1. **developer** configures a harness to start parley mcp --workspace demo with the CLI's endpoint and credential
2. **agent** lists the tools, calls activity and then fork_create
3. **parley CLI** runs each command's own run step in its process and answers with what the command prints
4. **agent** calls code_mode with one script that commits two files with scm_commit on the fork, opens the change with change_open and lands it with change_land with wait set, and returns the landed sha
5. **parley CLI** runs the script, makes its three tool calls, writes one line per call to stderr and answers with what the script returned
6. **parleyd** serves the same requests the shell commands make and lands the change

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the built parley binary, agentkit-go's runner, code mode and MCP server, a hub of hubtest with its repositories, the command tree of internal/cli

**Setup:**

- a hub with the repository demo, as the land tests of test/e2e start it, and the parley binary built without cgo

**End state:**

- the script's result holds the sha of demo's main, which holds the two files
- the change is landed
- the process's stderr holds one line per tool call, five in all, and none holds a file's content
- the hub's audit holds, for this credential, the requests the shell commands activity, fork create, scm commit, change open and change land make, in that order

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/cli_test.go: session over mcp.CommandTransport of `parley mcp --workspace demo`; CallTool(activity); CallTool(fork_create {name: "t1"}); CallTool(code_mode {script}); assert the end state through the hub's API
```

### PATH-2: One script works in a sandbox and on the hub

1. **developer** starts parley mcp --workspace demo--fix --sandbox <id> for a fork whose sandbox has tools
2. **parley CLI** reads the sandbox's tools from the hub and serves them beside the command tools and code_mode
3. **agent** calls code_mode with a script that runs search_files and edit_file in the sandbox, execute to run the tests, then change_show on the hub, and returns the change's state
4. **parleyd** relays each sandbox tool call into the sandbox and answers the hub command
5. **OpenShell gateway** runs the tool server once per sandbox tool call

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the built parley binary, agentkit-go's runner, code mode and MCP server, a hub of hubtest with the sandbox tool routes, the fake runtime with host directories and the stand-in tool server

**Setup:**

- the hub of the sandbox tools tests of test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go (startSandboxToolsHub), with a change open on the fork

**End state:**

- the tool list holds the hub's thirteen sandbox tools between the command tools and code_mode
- the script returned the change's state
- the file edit_file changed holds the edit
- the hub holds three parley.sandbox.tool_call events for the sandbox, with via rest

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/sandbox_use_test.go: session over mcp.CommandTransport of `parley mcp --workspace <fork> --sandbox <id>` with the fork's token; CallTool(code_mode {script}); assert the end state as the sandbox tools tests do
```

### PATH-3: A read-only assistant, and a refused selection

1. **developer** starts parley mcp --read-only
2. **agent** lists the tools and reads a change with change_show
3. **parley CLI** serves only the commands whose route is a GET, change_land not among them
4. **developer** starts parley mcp --groups admin
5. **parley CLI** prints a usage_error naming admin and exits 2

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the built parley binary, agentkit-go's runner and MCP server, a hub of hubtest

**Setup:**

- a hub with the repository demo and one change

**End state:**

- the read-only session listed change_show and no change_land, scm_commit or fork_create
- change_show answered the change
- parley mcp --groups admin exited 2 with one usage_error envelope on stderr and nothing on stdout

**Pseudocode:**

```
a new test in test/e2e/cli_test.go: session over `parley mcp --read-only`; ListTools; CallTool(change_show); then run `parley mcp --groups admin` and read its exit status and streams
```

- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `09` — declares parley mcp through the command helper and reads every command's declaration, flags and JSON help, the settings resolution, the error envelopes and the exit codes
- `56` — calls GET …/sandboxes/:id/tools and POST …/sandboxes/:id/tools/:name for --sandbox, and uses its stand-in tool server in the end-to-end test

### 1. Select the commands and print them as tools with parley mcp --list (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-2.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-2.3

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the selection's and the definitions' behaviours to a new internal/cli/mcp_test.go, with probe commands added through options.extra where a rule needs a command the real tree lacks, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Declare parley mcp with declare, auth user, with the flags --list, --groups (default activity,change,claim,fork,land,sandbox,scm,workspace:read), --read-only, --workspace, --sandbox, --no-code-mode and --script-timeout, and add it to the root. With --list it needs neither an endpoint nor a credential unless --sandbox is given
- 1.3 Keep with each command what its tool needs and the JSON help does not show: whether it shows a secret once (the declaration's ShowsOnce), and a new mark of the declaration for a command that needs a terminal or runs until interrupted, set on sandbox shell and events tail, and one for a flag that makes its command run until interrupted, set on the follow flag of sandbox logs
- 1.4 Read --groups: each element is a group name or name:read; a never-served group (admin, keys, tokens, secrets, login, credential-helper, help, version, mcp) is a usage_error naming it; an unknown name, an empty element or another suffix is a usage_error listing the names that may be given
- 1.5 Select the commands of the named groups, those of a :read group and all of them under --read-only only when their method is GET, and drop by rule every command whose auth is admin or none, that shows a secret once or that carries the terminal mark, whatever group it is in
- 1.6 Make each selected command a tool definition: the name from its words, the description, and an input schema that is an object without additional properties, with one string per argument and one typed parameter per flag, named as the PRD's decision 14 says, without api-key, endpoint-url, json, poll-interval and the flags marked as running until interrupted; required as the command requires them
- 1.7 With --workspace, make the parameters of the arguments slug, workspace-slug, WORKSPACE and parent optional and remember the workspace as their default
